name: Hobart
name_evidence: Wikivoyage "Hobart" page (See/Do listings) and Discover Tasmania "things to do in Hobart"; a state capital and headline city (rank 1-2 exemption not needed: 20 kept spots).

spots.name: Museum of Old and New Art
spots.bio: A private contemporary art museum at Berriedale on the Derwent, reached by ferry from Brooke Street Pier or by road.

spots.name: Kunanyi / Mount Wellington
spots.bio: A 1,271 m peak above Hobart with a road to the summit, lookouts and walking tracks.

spots.name: Salamanca Place
spots.bio: A row of convict-era sandstone warehouses on the waterfront, now galleries, craft shops, bars and restaurants.

spots.name: Battery Point
spots.bio: A historic Georgian suburb of steep lanes, Arthur Circus and old cottages, best explored on foot.

spots.name: Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery
spots.bio: The state museum in the city centre, with Tasmanian art, natural history and an Antarctic exhibition, free to enter.

spots.name: Cascades Female Factory
spots.bio: A former convict women's prison in South Hobart, part of the UNESCO convict sites, with guided heritage tours.

spots.name: Sullivans Cove
spots.bio: Hobart's original landing point and working waterfront, home to Constitution Dock and the Sydney to Hobart finish.

spots.name: Cascade Brewery
spots.bio: Australia's oldest brewery, in the foothills of South Hobart, with brewery and tasting tours.

spots.name: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.bio: A rescue sanctuary at Brighton where you meet kangaroos, wombats, koalas and Tasmanian devils on daily tours.

spots.name: Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens
spots.bio: Botanic gardens established in 1818 on the Queens Domain, with a conservatory and the seasonal Lily Pads display.

spots.name: Richmond
spots.bio: Australia's oldest colonial village in the Coal River valley, with convict-built sandstone streets and tea rooms.

spots.name: Richmond Bridge
spots.bio: A convict-built sandstone bridge of 1823, said to be Australia's oldest bridge still in use, free to visit.

spots.name: Richmond Gaol
spots.bio: Australia's oldest surviving convict gaol, used from 1825 to 1840 and now open to visitors.

spots.name: Maritime Museum of Tasmania
spots.bio: Tasmania's largest maritime collection, covering whaling, lighthouses and boatbuilding, in the city centre.

spots.name: Penitentiary Chapel
spots.bio: A convict-era chapel and criminal court with solitary cells, visited on guided day tours and night ghost tours.

spots.name: Narryna Heritage Museum
spots.bio: An 1830s merchant's house in Battery Point, furnished with decorative arts and set in a garden.

spots.name: Shot Tower
spots.bio: An 1870 sandstone shot tower at Taroona with 259 wooden steps up to views over the Derwent estuary.

spots.name: Mount Nelson
spots.bio: A hill with a lookout, signal station and picnic area looking over Hobart and the Derwent.

spots.name: Kingston Beach
spots.bio: A sandy suburban beach on the Derwent at Kingston, with a beachside art hub.

spots.name: Glenorchy Art and Sculpture Park
spots.bio: A free waterside sculpture park on the Derwent at Glenorchy, on Hobart's northern fringe, with a walking path.

name: Huon Valley
name_evidence: Wikivoyage has a "Huon Valley" page and the region is branded "Huon Trail" by Tasmanian tourism; the named region is proposed rather than the town Huonville (COVERAGE: prefer the region travellers name).

spots.name: Hartz Mountains National Park
spots.bio: An alpine plateau of glacial lakes and peaks above the Huon Valley, reached by a road from Geeveston.

spots.name: Tahune Forest AirWalk
spots.bio: A 597 m elevated walkway through the forest canopy above the Huon River at Tahune Reserve.

spots.name: Hastings Caves
spots.bio: Guided dolomite caves with the Newdegate Cave tour and a thermal pool fed by mineral springs.

spots.name: Hartz Peak
spots.bio: The highest point of Hartz Mountains National Park, reached by a three to five hour return walk.

spots.name: Huonville
spots.bio: The Huon Valley's regional centre on the Huon River, a base for the Mount Misery and Scenic Hill walks.

spots.name: Geeveston
spots.bio: The Huon Valley's southern visitor town, gateway to Tahune and Hartz Mountains.

spots.name: Cygnet
spots.bio: A Huon Valley arts town on the Channel, with galleries and cafes along the Huon Trail.

spots.name: Lake Esperance
spots.bio: A glacial lake in Hartz Mountains National Park, reached by a boardwalk loop.

spots.name: Arve Falls
spots.bio: A short walk from Hartz Road to a waterfall in Hartz Mountains National Park.

name: Bruny Island
name_evidence: Wikivoyage "Bruny Island" page, parks.tas.gov.au and a Tasmanian tourism brand; a car-ferry island day trip with 44,614 Wikipedia views and 3 counted sources.

spots.name: South Bruny National Park
spots.bio: Coastal forest, heath and lighthouse in three sections on South Bruny, with walks and wildlife.

spots.name: Cape Bruny Lighthouse
spots.bio: An 1836 lighthouse at the far end of Bruny Island, Australia's second oldest, with grounds open to visitors.

spots.name: The Hummock
spots.bio: A hilltop platform with a wide view over The Neck isthmus, a must-see stop on Bruny Island.

spots.name: Adventure Bay
spots.bio: A sheltered bay and beach on South Bruny where the island's tours depart.

spots.name: Fluted Cape
spots.bio: A 4 km coastal walk to Fluted Cape, popular for wildlife, in South Bruny National Park.

spots.name: Grass Point
spots.bio: An easy track along the water at Adventure Bay to a former whaling station in South Bruny National Park.

spots.name: East Cloudy Head
spots.bio: A 12 km return trail to the East Cloudy Head cliffs, with views over the Southern Ocean.

spots.name: Cloudy Bay
spots.bio: A long windswept beach on the south-west coast of Bruny Island, popular with surfers.

name: Mount Field National Park
name_evidence: Wikivoyage "Mount Field National Park" page and parks.tas.gov.au; Tasmania's first national park (1916) and Russell Falls is a headline attraction.

spots.name: Russell Falls
spots.bio: A twin cascade reached by a short track from the Mount Field visitor centre.

spots.name: Tarn Shelf
spots.bio: An alpine plateau of tarns and lakes, reached by a long day walk from Lake Dobson.

spots.name: Lake Dobson
spots.bio: A glacial tarn at the end of the Lake Dobson road, a destination for snow and short walks.

name: Southwest National Park
name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Southwest National Park' ('accounting for 10% of Tasmania'); Wikipedia; Parks Tasmania.

spots.name: Gordon Dam
spots.bio: A 140 m-high arch dam at Strathgordon with a lookout over Lake Gordon and the Gordon River gorge.

spots.name: Lake Pedder
spots.bio: A large lake in the Southwest National Park with a lodge on its shore, viewed from lookouts and by boat.

spots.name: South Coast Track
spots.bio: An 85 km coastal walk through the park's wild south coast, usually six to eight days one way.

name: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
name_evidence: Wikivoyage page 'Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park' ('The main draw of the park is Nelson Falls'); Parks Tasmania national park; Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.

spots.name: Nelson Falls
spots.bio: A roughly 30 m waterfall on the Nelson River, reached by a short boardwalk walk off the Lyell Highway.

spots.name: Frenchmans Cap Track
spots.bio: A hard 3-5 day walk from the Lyell Highway to the white quartzite summit of Frenchmans Cap.

spots.name: Donaghys Hill Lookout
spots.bio: A 30-40 minute return walk to a wilderness lookout over the Franklin River Valley.

spots.name: Franklin River
spots.bio: A wild river in the World Heritage area, famed for guided multi-day rafting expeditions through its gorges.

name: West Coast Tasmania
name_evidence: Discover Tasmania has a 'West Coast' regional page (https://www.discovertasmania.com.au/regions/west-coast, a counted source for Strahan); Wikivoyage 'Strahan' calls it 'the regional hub of the West Coast' and Wikivoyage 'Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park' says 'in the West Coast of Tasmania'; Wikipedia 'West Coast, Tasmania'. Wikivoyage has no West Coast page of its own (only 'Western Tasmania'), so the name rests on the tourism-board region; owner to confirm the display name (e.g. 'West Coast Tasmania' to avoid NZ West Coast).

spots.name: Sarah Island
spots.bio: The ruins of an 1822 convict penal station on a Macquarie Harbour island, visited on a cruise from Strahan.

spots.name: Gordon River
spots.bio: A rainforest river in Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park, visited by cruise from Strahan.

spots.name: Strahan
spots.bio: A Macquarie Harbour fishing port with a historic waterfront and foreshore walk, the base for Gordon River cruises.

spots.name: Queenstown
spots.bio: A former copper-mining town ringed by bare mined hills, with a historic main street and mine tours.

spots.name: Ocean Beach
spots.bio: A 40 km surf beach of huge dunes and Southern Ocean swell north-west of Strahan, with dangerous swimming.

spots.name: Montezuma Falls
spots.bio: Tasmania's highest waterfall at over 104 m, reached by an 11.5 km return walk along an old tramway.

spots.name: Iron Blow Lookout
spots.bio: A lookout over the Iron Blow, the huge mine pit above Queenstown where the area's mining began.

spots.name: Zeehan
spots.bio: A former silver-mining boomtown whose single main street keeps many of its civic and heritage buildings.

spots.name: West Coast Heritage Centre
spots.bio: A small museum on Zeehan's Main Street about life on Tasmania's West Coast in the early 20th century.

spots.name: Hogarth Falls
spots.bio: A small cascade reached by a 30-minute rainforest walk from People's Park at the north end of Strahan Harbour.
